trans-unit.target: This gallery will be permanently deleted, with its medias and all of their files. This cannot be undone. Continue?
Changing the slug moves the media public URL, a redirect will be set up automatically. Continue?
Changing the title will change the category's URL (slug), a redirect will be automatically set up. Continue?
A gallery is a category of media: name it, drop your photographs on it, and it is online.
One gallery holds no photo of its own: it gathers what the others have just received.
Caption, credits, and the video a media can open on.
Order the media, choose the one representing the gallery, and edit several of them at once.
A selection leaves for another gallery with its files, its pages redirecting to where it now sits.
The site hands the originals back as one archive, and keeps a trash of its own for the photos.
Deleting a gallery only takes it off the site: everything it holds waits in the trash.
It has nothing to publish: it is visible the moment it exists, and the view on site button opens it.
Several files at once, each becoming a media of the gallery - the sizes shown are what the server accepts.
The creation form carries the first batch of media too, so a gallery is created and filled in one go.
Every gallery of the site is listed here, in the order they are displayed in.
The title is what the site shows, and the address of the gallery is built from it.
Every media of the batch takes this name, numbered - each one is retouched afterwards, one by one.
The media added over the last days, all galleries taken together, and each thumbnail names the gallery it really belongs to.

Two settings of the gallery group decide it: the number of days it goes back, and how many photos it shows at most. When the window catches nothing, it falls back on the last day carrying an addition.
It offers no upload, no reordering and no cover: it holds nothing of its own to arrange.
"Latest additions" is among them, written by the site the first time the galleries are listed - it is a gallery like the others, which can be renamed and moved.
Credits, rights, download and move to trash act on the checked photos where they actually sit - which is how a whole day's upload is credited in one go.
Changing it here moves this one photo, its files following it - a whole selection is moved from the gallery screen instead ("Move photos to another gallery").
Shown with the media on the site - the same value can be written on a whole selection from the gallery.
The media's own address is changed behind the padlock only, and the old one keeps redirecting to the new one.
Its media are listed under its form.
A media is always reached from the gallery holding it.
It opens the only screen a media has - saving it brings you back here.
It is shown under the media and stands for it aloud in a screen reader; retouching it moves no address.
Paste the address of the page you were watching it on, the platform reads itself off it; the field below uploads the site's own copy instead.
The media representing the gallery wherever it is shown - left unpicked, a random one is taken each time.
The order and the cover are stored as you go; only the gallery's own fields need the save button.
Its media are listed under its own form, which is where everything below happens.
The gallery to arrange is one of these - not "Latest additions", which holds no photo of its own and arranges nothing.
Check the media, then write the same credits on all of them, mark them as rights reserved, download them in high resolution or as originals, or move them to the trash in one go.
Drag a media by its handle: the new order is saved the moment you drop it, with nothing to validate.
A batch at a time, always from the gallery holding them - a media is never created on its own.
The old page of each photo redirects to its new address, the gallery left behind closes the gap in its order, and its cover is released if it was one of them.
Its media are listed under its form, and the move is done from there.
The files follow into the arrival gallery's own directory, and the photos land after what it already holds.
Start from the gallery holding the photos to move, not from the one receiving them.
A few photos or the whole gallery - they are moved in the order the grid shows them.
Every gallery holding photos of its own is offered, except the one you are looking at and "Latest additions", which holds none. The last entry creates one: its name is asked for right next to it.
Left empty the photos keep the titles they had; filled, they are numbered from where the arrival gallery leaves off - "Cars 12" becoming "Volvo 3".
One zip for the selection: the high resolution kept by the site, or the originals as they were uploaded when the gallery was told to keep them. A selection past 1 GB is refused, its size stated.
Its media are listed under its form.
The files are handed back from the gallery holding them.
The whole gallery at once, or the few photos you are after.
Each gallery carries its own, under its form as soon as a photo is put there: the same downloads are offered, and "Restore" hands the photos back to the gallery at the end of it.
The button asks first, then moves the gallery to the trash: its media, its files and its address are all kept, and only its own page answers "gone" from then on.
Dropping a gallery for good is the other button of the trash, held at the administrator: it is the only one that removes the files from the server.
The galleries the site is showing right now.
It comes back where it was, with its media and its position, and its address starts answering again.
The button above the list switches between the galleries online and the ones set aside - the same screen, showing the other side.
An art edition has just been paid for: %numbers%.
Print the certificates from the print orders screen, sign them, post them, then release the order to the lab.
Its certificate of authenticity, signed and numbered by hand, reaches you separately by post.
Your print is number %numbers% of the edition.
The gallery stays in the back-office but leaves every public page - the index, the blocks, the menus, the sitemap - and its photographs leave the automatic galleries with it.
Left empty, the print is unlimited. A number opens a numbered edition and writes its register. Careful: once saved it can no longer be changed.
The photograph stays in the back-office but leaves every public page. Better than deleting what is worth keeping and not worth showing.
Offers this photograph for order. Which sizes depends on its original: those whose proportions and pixels it has.
300 for a print looked at closely. 200 is enough for a large one hung on a wall, and opens the sale to smaller files.
Long edge an original must reach to be offered at this size. Below it, the photograph is simply not offered that size.
The code the lab gives this product. The only column to rewrite if you change lab.
What an order already placed remembers this format by. Renaming it does not affect past sales, but avoid it once prints have been sold.
Show the link to the category
Grid of the gallery's categories, one thumbnail each.
Grid of a category's photos and videos.
Applied to every media in this batch
Select every file to add at once — up to %files% files, %size% MB each, %total% MB in total
The uploaded files are kept outside the site, exactly as sent
Shared title, numbered for each media of this batch. Left empty, each title falls back to its filename.
Stamps the site's signature into a corner of every photo of the batch. Both signatures (for light and dark backgrounds) are uploaded from Site graphics.
Leave empty to use the corner set for the whole site.
The edition is already open: its size can no longer be changed.

The address of the page the video is watched on, as it appears in the browser's bar - it is turned into a privacy-first embed url when saved. YouTube, TikTok, Vimeo and Dailymotion are recognized; any other embed url is kept as it was pasted.
The caption read under the media on its page — leave it empty when there is nothing to say
Forms the media public URL. Posed once at upload and no longer following the title: editing it here sets up a redirect from the old URL. Emptied, it is rebuilt from the title.
Used as the page title and as the image alternative text. Editing it does not move the media URL.
Only applies to a new file sent above: a file already stored carries the signature it was given, and stamping it again would lay a second one over the first.
These medias will be moved to the trash: they leave the site, but their files are kept and you will be able to restore them. Continue?
Permanently delete the selected medias and their files? This cannot be undone.
No file to download for this selection: the originals were not kept at upload, or the files are no longer on the server

Displayed above the grid, and reused as the page's description for search engines and social networks (truncated to 150 characters for the latter).
The batch was too large for the server and nothing was uploaded. Add the files in smaller batches, or raise post_max_size.

%name% weighs %size% MB, the limit is %limit% MB per file.
%count% files selected, %limit% at a time at most — add the rest in a second upload.
A video hosted by the site and played by the browser: no third party, so no consent to ask for. mp4, webm or ogg, %size% MB at most. It wins over the url above when both are filled in.

Media categories, they are the site's gallery. "Uncategorized" is a fallback and can't be deleted. Create or edit a category, reorder their display position and add media to them. Moving one to the trash only takes it off the site: the button above the list shows what is waiting there, and puts it back.
Moves the gallery to the trash: it leaves the site straight away, but its photographs and their files stay untouched and you can restore it from the galleries trash

The category's media, click one of them to change its file, caption or credits, or check several of them to delete them in one go. Drag them to reorder them and pick the one representing the category, both being saved as you go.

%count% media added over the last days, all galleries taken together, grouped by day. Each photo belongs to the gallery named under its thumbnail: credits, rights, download and move to trash apply where it actually sits.
No media added yet: this gallery fills itself as soon as another one receives photos.
This category has no media yet.
Medias moved to trash: they are off the site, but their files are kept. Check some to restore them, or to delete them permanently.
The trash of this category is empty.
Change this media's file, caption, credits, type or position, or move it to another category.

Watermark: photos can be stamped with the site's signature as a batch of media is added, burnt into the pixels of every size generated. Both signatures (for light and dark backgrounds) are uploaded from Site graphics; the corner, width and margin are set in Configuration, group General (Watermark - Corner, Width, Margin).
The sizes on sale, their prices and the lab's reference
The prints ordered, those the lab is printing and those waiting for your signature

The order is on its way to the lab again.
Prints are in test mode: no order will actually be printed or shipped.
This print is no longer offered.
This gallery's QR code, to print on a card, a flyer or an exhibition label.
Ideally close to the title (no accents, capitals or spaces). Editable via the lock icon; a redirect preserves SEO.
